title: New Orleans men in New York: Sig Norelli and Napoleon
summary: They find few New Orleans players in New York and discuss Norelli and Napoleon.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: By that time, there were very few New Orleans men in the picture around New York. I can't, offhand, I can't remember anybody from New Orleans. There were some here in Chicago, but I can't recall in New York there being any New Orleans men.
No, I can't, or in the Goldkitt group. Yeah. We're undoubtedly missing one or two, but I can't think who they'd be.
Steve Brown, of course, when he's missing Goldkitt. But they had dissipated by that time. There were some around Chicago, but not many in New York.
Well, Sig Norelli was around New York. Oh, yes.
Is he from New Orleans? I don't know, because I always associated him with that group.

So Napoleon was, wasn't he? With, yeah, no, no. Napoleon and Sig Norelli, I think, are New York Italian boys. They're not from New Orleans. No, it's true that they certainly do play Dixieland style, but I don't think they're of New Orleans origin at all.
